Operator Behaviors

Operator Behaviors provide a pipeline stage for conditional value handling after resolve and merge but before filtering, reduction, and taps. Operators act on the fully resolved pipeline value and determine whether that value should continue through the remaining stages.

The Operator Stage runs after resolve and merge, receiving the merged pipeline value as input. An operator may forward the value unchanged, forward a modified value, or suppress the update entirely. Operators do not mutate existing state and do not emit snapshots directly.

Operators are commonly used for deduplication, conditional suppression, and value normalization that must occur before filters or reducers execute. When an operator returns VAULT_NOOP, the current pipeline execution is short-circuited for that value, no snapshot is emitted, and downstream stages are skipped.

Asynchronous Execution

Operator behaviors execute asynchronously and are awaited by the pipeline. This allows operators to perform asynchronous checks or comparisons while preserving strict execution order and non-overlapping pipeline runs.

Operator Stage

The Operator Stage executes after resolve and merge and before filters, reducers, and taps. Operators receive the fully resolved and merged pipeline value and determine whether that value should continue through the remaining pipeline stages.

Operators may forward the value unchanged, forward a modified value, or suppress further pipeline processing. Suppression occurs when an operator returns VAULT_NOOP, which immediately ends pipeline execution for the current value. Downstream stages are skipped and no snapshot is emitted. The pipeline resumes normally for future executions.

Operators do not mutate existing state, do not emit snapshots directly, and do not influence pipeline scheduling or lifecycle control. Their responsibility is limited to evaluating the resolved pipeline value and deciding whether, and in what form, that value proceeds to later stages.

Core Pipeline Stage

The Operator stage is a core pipeline stage and is always present as part of the FeatureCell lifecycle. However, individual operator behaviors are not applied implicitly. Operators are attached explicitly through the fluent .operators() API during FeatureCell initialization.

Operator configuration is declarative and ordered. When provided, operators are executed in the Processing Layer in the exact order they are registered. This ensures that value refinement, suppression, and deduplication rules are defined explicitly at startup rather than embedded into static cell configuration or implicit runtime behavior.

Operators are evaluated deterministically for each pipeline execution. They operate in isolation, receive no direct access to state history or reducers, and may not perform side effects. This ensures that operator behavior remains predictable and does not introduce hidden coupling between pipeline stages.

Fluent Operators() API

A FeatureCell may declare multiple operators. The fluent .operators() API accepts an array of operator behaviors, which is treated as a declarative, ordered configuration. When provided, operators execute in the Processing Layer in the exact order they are listed during initialization.

Each operator receives the resolved and merged pipeline value produced by earlier stages and determines whether that value should continue through the pipeline. Operators may forward the value unchanged, forward a modified value, or suppress the update entirely.

An empty operator array is ignored and has no effect on pipeline execution.

Note

Although operator composition is fully supported, operator chains should remain narrowly focused. Because operators may suppress emissions or alter values before reduction, combining multiple operators with overlapping concerns can make pipeline behavior harder to reason about. Operators are most effective when each enforces a single, clearly defined transformation or suppression rule.

Diagrams
Available Operator Behaviors
FeatureCell Initialization

The Operator stage exposes a fluent configuration API that allows engineers to register operator behaviors during FeatureCell initialization.

This API does not execute operators directly. It records an ordered set of operator behaviors that are later applied by the Operator stage during pipeline execution.

Fluent Operator Configuration
Fluent API Description

.operators(operators)

input:

  • operators: OperatorsBehaviorClassContract<T>[]

returns: FeatureCellBaseShape (chainable)

Registers operator behaviors for a FeatureCell. The supplied behaviors define how resolved and merged pipeline values may be refined, suppressed, or deduplicated before reaching downstream stages.

Operators are executed in the Processing Layer in the exact order they are registered. This method must be called before initialize(). Multiple calls overwrite prior operator configuration.

Examples

Operators are enabled by registering operator behaviors during FeatureCell initialization.

Example 1: Configure a FeatureCell with Operators

In this example, the withDistinctUntilChanged operator is registered during initialization. Operators are executed in the order they are declared and operate on the resolved, merged pipeline value before downstream stages are evaluated. 

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[][]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[][]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Apply one or more operators during initialization
    this.vault
      .operators(
        [
          withDistinctUntilChanged()
          // up to N operators
        ]
      ).initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Operator behaviors are registered via the fluent API,
    // not as part of the declarative FeatureCell definition.
  ]
);

// Apply one or more operators during initialization
employeeCell.operators(
  [
    withDistinctUntilChanged()
    // up to N operators
  ]
).initialize();`}}
